question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. The new manager B. is responsible of C. the entire marketing D. campaign.
solution_text:
The correct answer is is responsible of..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective “responsible” is always followed by the preposition “for”, not “of”.

• The correct phrase is “is responsible for”, so the part “is responsible of” contains the grammatical error.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Fixed preposition: responsible + for (a task/thing) and responsible + to (a person). SSC frequently tests such preposition collocations.

• Example: “She is responsible for the entire marketing campaign.”

 

NOTE

• “The new manager”, “the entire marketing” and “campaign.” are all grammatically correct and carry no error.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrase:

As the deadline approached, the team was working _____ to finalize the report
solution_text:
The correct answer is against the clock..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom “against the clock” means to work hurriedly because there is very little time left.

• As the deadline approached, the team was rushing to finish, so “working against the clock” fits perfectly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• against the clock = racing to finish before a deadline / time limit.

• Example: “The doctors worked against the clock to save the patient.”

 

NOTE

• “under wraps” = kept secret; “around the corner” = about to happen/nearby; “in high spirits” = very cheerful – none conveys the sense of hurrying due to a deadline.

question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Hapless
solution_text:
The correct answer is Unlucky..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Hapless” means unfortunate or having no luck; therefore its closest synonym is “Unlucky”.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Hapless = unlucky, unfortunate, luckless.

• Root: “hap” = luck/chance; “-less” = without → without luck.

• Example: “The hapless traveller missed every train.”

 

NOTE

• “Fortunate”, “Lucky” and “Successful” are antonyms of hapless, expressing good luck or achievement.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate idiom:

She took the criticism _____ and used it to improve her performance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is in stride..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom “take something in stride” means to deal with a difficulty calmly and without being upset.

• She accepted the criticism calmly and used it to improve, so “in stride” fits best.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• take in stride = handle a problem or setback without letting it disturb you.

• Example: “He took the sudden change in plans in stride.”

 

NOTE

• “at face value” = accept as it appears; “with a grain of salt” = with scepticism; “out of context” = without proper background – none conveys calmly accepting and using the criticism.

question:
Which of the following sentences uses the word "saw" with the same meaning as in the following sentence?

"He saw the car coming too late"
option_1: She used a hand saw to cut the plank in half.
option_2: We needed a power saw to cut through the thick branch.
option_3: I saw a beautiful sunset last night.
option_4: The lumberjack's saw was very loud.
solution_text:
The correct answer is I saw a beautiful sunset last night..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In “He saw the car coming too late”, “saw” is the past tense of the verb “see” (to perceive with the eyes).

• “I saw a beautiful sunset last night” uses “saw” in exactly the same sense – the past tense of ‘see’.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• “saw” as a verb = past tense of see; “saw” as a noun = a cutting tool.

• Such questions test the same part of speech and meaning (homographs).

 

NOTE

• In options 1, 2 and 4, “saw” is a noun referring to the cutting tool, not the act of seeing.

question:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on it:

Online purchasing, which combines unmatched ease with a distinct set of disadvantages, has completely changed how consumers behave. Accessibility is its main benefit; customers may explore and buy things from almost anywhere at any time, and there is frequently a greater selection than in physical stores. Important lures include competitive pricing, made possible by internet retailers' reduced overhead, and the simplicity of comparing prices from several providers. However, there are significant drawbacks to online shopping's virtual nature. Delivery-related discontent may result from the inability to personally inspect things before purchase. Concerns over shipping delays, unstated expenses, and the effects of packaging and transportation on the environment are becoming more widespread. Additionally, the individualised customer service experience may be weakened by a lack of human interaction.

 

What is the primary advantage of online purchasing according to the text?
option_1: It allows for in-person inspection of products
option_2: It provides easy access to a wider selection of items from anywhere at any time
option_3: It offers higher prices than physical stores
option_4: It eliminates the need for shipping
solution_text:
The correct answer is It provides easy access to a wider selection of items from anywhere at any time..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states, “Accessibility is its main benefit; customers may explore and buy things from almost anywhere at any time, and there is frequently a greater selection than in physical stores.”

• This directly identifies easy access to a wider selection anytime, anywhere as the primary advantage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• In RC, the “primary/main” advantage is usually stated explicitly – here signalled by “main benefit”.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 is a drawback (inability to inspect); Option 3 contradicts the passage (it mentions competitive/lower pricing); Option 4 is false as shipping concerns are discussed.

question: Choose the correctly spelt word:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bureaucrat..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is “Bureaucrat” – spelt B-U-R-E-A-U-C-R-A-T.

• It comes from “bureau” (office) + “crat” (ruler/power).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Bureaucrat = an official who works by fixed rules of a bureaucracy.

• Remember the base word “bureau” to fix the tricky “-eau-” spelling.

 

NOTE

• “Beaurocrat”, “Burocrat” and “Buroucrat” are all misspellings of the word.

question: Choose the correctly spelt word:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Irresistible..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is “Irresistible” – double ‘r’ and ending in “-ible”.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

• Irresistible = too attractive or tempting to be resisted.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: As thick as thieves
solution_text:
The correct answer is Very close and loyal..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom “as thick as thieves” means to be very close, intimate and loyal friends who share secrets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• as thick as thieves = extremely friendly and trusting of each other.

• Example: “The two sisters are as thick as thieves.”

 

NOTE

• “Very secretive”, “Very sneaky” and “Very quiet” misinterpret the idiom; it refers to closeness, not secrecy or slyness.

question:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

A person who studies birds
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ornithologist..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The study of birds is called “ornithology”, so a person who studies birds is an “Ornithologist”.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Ornithology = study of birds (Greek ‘ornis’ = bird).

• Related: Entomologist (insects), Ichthyologist (fish).

 

NOTE

• A Biologist studies life in general, an Ecologist studies ecosystems, and a Zoologist studies animals broadly – none specifically studies birds.

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Felicity
solution_text:
The correct answer is Misery..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Felicity” means intense happiness or great joy; its opposite is “Misery” (a state of great suffering or unhappiness).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Felicity = happiness, bliss. Antonyms include misery, unhappiness, woe.

 

NOTE

• “Despair”, “Sorrow” and “Anger” are negative emotions but “Misery” is the most direct and complete antonym of happiness, i.e. felicity.

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Repudiate
solution_text:
The correct answer is Accept..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Repudiate” means to reject or refuse to accept something; therefore its antonym is “Accept”.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Repudiate = reject, deny, disown, renounce.

• Example: “He repudiated the false allegations.”

 

NOTE

• “Reject”, “Disown” and “Deny” are synonyms of repudiate, not antonyms.

question:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

A place where records and documents are stored
solution_text:
The correct answer is Archive..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An “Archive” is a place where historical records and important documents are collected and stored.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Archive = a collection of historical documents or records, or the place housing them.

 

NOTE

• A “Library” chiefly stores books for reading; “Storage” is a general space for keeping any goods; a “Depository” is where things (often valuables/goods) are deposited – “Archive” best fits records and documents specifically.

question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

Let the emergency meeting be convened at 10 AM without delay.
option_1: Convene the emergency meeting at 10 AM without delay.
option_2: The emergency meeting should be convened at 10 AM without delay.
option_3: They will convene the emergency meeting at 10 AM without delay
option_4: An emergency meeting is convened at 10 AM without delay.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Convene the emergency meeting at 10 AM without delay..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Let + object + be + past participle” is the passive form of an imperative/command.

• Its active form is a direct imperative beginning with the base verb: “Convene the emergency meeting at 10 AM without delay.”

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Passive imperative → Active imperative: “Let the door be closed” → “Close the door.”

 

NOTE

• Options 2 and 4 remain passive (“be convened” / “is convened”); Option 3 adds a subject “They will”, changing it to a future statement rather than the active imperative.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.

The company CEO announced, "We will not be able to meet the deadline for this quarter, which is a great disappointment for all of us, but we will have to work harder next time."
option_1: The company CEO announced that they will not be able to meet the deadline for this quarter, which is a great disappointment for all of us, but that they will have to work harder next time.
option_2: The company CEO announced that they would not be able to meet the deadline for this quarter, which was a great disappointment for all of them, but that they would have to work harder the next time.
option_3: The company CEO announced that they would not be able to meet the deadline for that quarter, which was a great disappointment for all of them, but that they would work harder next time.
option_4: The company CEO announced that they would not be able to meet the deadline for that quarter, which was a great disappointment for all of them, but that they would have to work harder the next time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The company CEO announced that they would not be able to meet the deadline for that quarter, which was a great disappointment for all of them, but that they would have to work harder the next time..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In indirect speech, “will” → “would”, “is” → “was”, “us” → “them”, “this quarter” → “that quarter”, and “next time” → “the next time”.

• Option 4 correctly applies all these back-shift and pronoun/time changes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Reported speech rules: present→past, will→would, near demonstratives/adverbs shift to distant forms (this→that, next→the next).

 

NOTE

• Option 1 keeps present tense (“will”, “is”) and “us”; Option 2 wrongly keeps “this quarter”; Option 3 drops “have to” and keeps “next time”, so all are incorrect.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

I am not one of these people who believes in rumours
solution_text:
The correct answer is believe..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the structure “one of those/these + plural noun + who + verb”, the relative pronoun “who” refers to the plural noun (“people”), so the verb must be plural: “believe”.

• Hence “...people who believe in rumours” is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Rule: “one of the + plural noun + who/that + plural verb.”

• Example: “He is one of those players who work hard.”

 

NOTE

• “believer” is a noun; “believing” and “to believe” are non-finite and do not agree with “who (people)” in this relative clause.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

The organized sellers with the ability to control their price-lines, or pass on any increase in cost to customers, should be able to maintain or improve profit margin.
option_1: should be able to maintain or improve profit margins
option_2: will be able to maintains or improve profit margin
option_3: will be able to maintain or improves profit margin
option_4: will be abled to maintain or improve profit margin
solution_text:
The correct answer is should be able to maintain or improve profit margins..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After “be able to”, the base form of the verb is used, so “maintain” and “improve” are correct.

• The plural “margins” suits the sense of the sellers keeping/raising their profit margins, giving the grammatically correct option.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• “be able to + base verb”; “abled” is not used in this construction.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 wrongly uses “maintains”; Option 3 wrongly uses “improves” after “to”; Option 4 uses the non-standard “be abled to” – all are grammatically incorrect.

question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

The students are completing their assignments.
option_1: The assignments are being completed by the students
option_2: The assignments are completed by the students
option_3: The assignments were completed by the students
option_4: The assignments have been completed by the students.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The assignments are being completed by the students..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is in the Present Continuous tense (are completing).

• Its passive form is “is/are + being + past participle” → “The assignments are being completed by the students.”

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Present Continuous passive: object + is/are being + V3 + by + subject.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 is simple present passive; Option 3 is simple past passive; Option 4 is present perfect passive – none matches the present continuous of the given sentence.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.

The captain explained that the ship had been sailing for three weeks and they had faced a severe storm the previous night.
option_1: The captain explained, "The ship was sailing for three weeks, and we faced a severe storm last night."
option_2: The captain explained, "The ship has been sailing for three weeks, and we had faced a severe storm last night."
option_3: The captain explained, "The ship has been sailing for three weeks, and we faced a severe storm last night."
option_4: The captain explained, "The ship had been sailing for three weeks, and we faced a severe storm last night."
solution_text:
The correct answer is The captain explained, "The ship has been sailing for three weeks, and we faced a severe storm last night.".

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Converting to direct speech, back-shifted tenses move forward: “had been sailing” → “has been sailing”, “had faced” → “faced”, “they” → “we”, and “the previous night” → “last night”.

• Option 3 applies all these changes correctly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Indirect → Direct: past perfect continuous → present perfect continuous; “the previous night” → “last night”.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 wrongly changes “had been sailing” to “was sailing”; Option 2 keeps “had faced”; Option 4 keeps “had been sailing” – all fail to restore the correct direct-speech tenses.

question:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. But the fleet was caught off guard as a sudden, strong storm blew in from the sea.

Q. Confident in their strategy to blockade the enemy port, the admiral gave the order for the ships to proceed.

R. The conflict became a desperate struggle for survival due to the unanticipated weather.

S. Without firing a shot, they were to cut off supplies and compel a surrender.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Q, S, P, R..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Q introduces the plan (the admiral orders the ships to proceed), S explains the strategy (cut off supplies without firing a shot), P brings the twist (but a storm caught the fleet off guard), and R gives the outcome (a desperate struggle for survival).

• The logical order is therefore Q-S-P-R.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Sequencing tips: the opening sentence sets the scene (Q), “But” (P) signals a contrast, and the result (R) comes last.

 

NOTE

• Orders P,S,Q,R / S,R,P,Q / R,S,P,Q break the cause-effect flow – e.g. starting with the contrast “But” or the outcome R makes the paragraph incoherent.

question:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. However, as the Empire grew, a series of internal and external pressures began to mount.

Q. The Roman Empire was the most powerful civilisation in history at its height.

R. Its gradual decline was caused by a confluence of political corruption, military overstretch, and economic instability.

S. Its vast network of roads, laws, and military outposts brought a period of peace and prosperity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Q, S, P, R..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Q introduces the topic (the powerful Roman Empire at its height), S describes its achievements (roads, laws, prosperity), P brings the turn with “However” (pressures began to mount), and R concludes with its decline.

• The coherent order is Q-S-P-R.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• The introductory sentence names the subject (Q); “However” (P) marks the shift to problems; the final result/decline (R) closes the paragraph.

 

NOTE

• Orders beginning with R or P (the decline or the contrast) place effects before their causes, breaking the logical progression, so the other options are incorrect.
